bib.title: Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2021 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks

read.skipped: Appendix figure axis residue and Khan Academy module lists (figures 9-15) are chart text only.

question: How well can machine learning models solve competition-level mathematics problems that need problem-solving heuristics rather than plug-and-chug calculation?
hypothesis: Scaling Transformers alone will not solve MATH; new algorithmic advances are needed.
contributions: MATH: 12,500 competition problems with step-by-step solutions and boxed answers
AMPS: a 23GB auxiliary mathematics pretraining corpus (Khan Academy + Mathematica)
Baselines with GPT-2 and GPT-3 showing low accuracy and slow scaling

method.summary: Builds MATH (7,500 train / 5,000 test problems from AMC/AIME-style contests, levels 1-5, 7 subjects, exact-match on \boxed{} answers) and AMPS pretraining corpus. GPT-2 models (0.1B-1.5B) are pretrained on AMPS then fine-tuned on MATH; GPT-3 is fine-tuned or few-shot via API.
method.task: competition mathematics answer generation, scored by exact match

datasets.name: MATH
datasets.source: AoPS contest archives (AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME and more); LaTeX + Asymptote
datasets.preprocessing: Final answers in \boxed{} with normalisation rules (simplified fractions, ignore spaces and units, equivalent fraction encodings)

datasets.name: AMPS Mathematica
datasets.size: around 5 million problems from 100 scripts (about 50,000 each); 37 scripts include step-by-step solutions
datasets.preprocessing: downsampled x2 in pretraining; AMPS total 23GB

models.name: GPT-2 (0.1B, 0.3B, 0.7B, 1.5B)
models.init_from: inferred: pretrained GPT-2 (natural-language), then AMPS pretraining

other.note: no AMPS pretraining (API limits); 13B fine-tuned via API, both few-shot

training.objective:
standard autoregressive language modelling; fine-tuning on equal mix of '

Final Answer: ' and '

Full Solution: ' sequences
training.epochs: 1 epoch AMPS pretraining; fine-tuning epochs not stated
training.compute: each run requires less than a day
training.wall_clock: less than a day per model

other.T5: two-week broad hyperparameter sweep, not competitive (tokenizer removes LaTeX symbols)

inference.decoding: GPT-2: HuggingFace default generation parameters plus beam search; beam 20 for final answer only, beam 10 for full solutions
inference.prompting:
GPT-2 prompted with '

Final Answer:'; GPT-3 few-shot prepends 8 problems with correct answers (no solutions)

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: exact match of normalised \boxed{} answer against ground truth

metrics.name: AUROC of confidence
metrics.definition: confidence = mean token probability of generated answer; probability a correct answer has higher confidence than an incorrect one

eval.protocol: Test set of 5,000; humans: 20 random test problems, 1 hour, by hand, 6 university students (4 are authors). Single run, no significance tests.

availability.data: MATH and AMPS released (Khan exercises code at github.com/Khan/khan-exercises)

limits: Models are 2021-era GPT-2/GPT-3; accuracy figures (3-7%) are long dated by later reasoning models (the target note cites MATH-500 at 97.3% for R1).
Single runs, no seeds, no significance tests; GPT-3 not AMPS-pretrained so comparisons confound pretraining.
Human study is 6 participants on 20 problems, 4 of them authors.
Fine-tuning learning rate, schedule, and epochs not stated.
Exact match on boxed answer; answers must follow strict formatting rules.
Authors concede scratch-space solutions hurt, hypothesised snowballing errors.

figures.caption: Previous work is based on formal theorem provers or straightforward plug-and-chug problems. Our dataset, MATH, has competition mathematics problems with step-by-step solutions written in LATEX and natural language.
